classification.difficultyReason: Translate equal area with a fixed base into equal perpendicular heights, then construct three different triangles satisfying that condition.

content.prompt: Draw three different triangles with the same base and the same area.

answer.short: Sample answer: use the same base $AB$ for three triangles whose opposite vertices lie on a line parallel to $AB$.
answer.worked:
Choose a base $AB=4\text{ cm}$. Place three different opposite vertices on a line $2\text{ cm}$ from $AB$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\tfrac12\times4\times2\\A&=4\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
All three triangles have the same base and perpendicular height.

spec.description: Authored sample construction: triangles ABC, ABD and ABE share AB and have opposite vertices on a parallel line.
spec.mathematics: AB=4 cm, common perpendicular height 2 cm; each area is 4 square centimetres.
